fixes: Show the inspection itself, because the headline's turn is 'people inspect' and nothing in the frame is inspecting. Lay the gold-flagged blade flat in the tray on a foam cutout, with the borescope's articulated tip (a knurled handpiece, a flexible sheath and a lit LED head, not three bare torus rings) aimed at its leading edge. Add a gloved hand cropped at the wrist holding the scope, or a loupe resting on the blade, so the gold mark reads as what the software flagged and the steel tool as the human check. Right now the blade stands upright in a block like a trophy. That reads as an award or a copy of frame 6's lone blade, not a part on the bench waiting to be inspected.

Build the primitives out and take the plate off the type. The blade is a flat tapered wedge. Give it a twisted airfoil, a fir-tree root, a platform and heat tint on the titanium, with the gold mark as a painted inspection band or tag instead of one edge strip. The gloves are flat cutout slabs. Model a slumped nitrile pair with fingers, creases and a contact shadow. The tray needs a rolled lip and a floor that isn't a black void. Behind the type, the big flat saturated wall reads as a coloured plate. Break it into hangar door panels with ribs and a light gradient from the open door, so the type sits in a real lit wall rather than on a rectangle.

Get the camera low and close on the bars so they fill at least half the frame, and crop out the flat window, white sill and blue wall band across the top third. Either seat the bars in the vise jaws or take the vise out. Give the stock milled detail: a chamfered edge, a fly cut face, tool marks and a crisp edge highlight.

Fix the chips: a doubled mirrored band floats inside the 70 ghost. Curl one set of helical chips falling from each cut face onto the plate with contact shadows. Give the glass ghosts refraction and edge caustics.

Make what the software puts out the subject, not a speck: a large gold anodized tag with a machined grommet wired to the turbine flange in the centre of the frame, or the two gold cased tools on the stand rail beside the open panel, so the headline tools has a body.

Finish the build: the stand is untextured square tube (gussets, bolt heads, chipped satin paint), the stand is cropped awkwardly and floats (contact shadows under casters), the open access panel does not show, break the uniform ribs with flanges, bolt rings and the heat tinted turbine.

Make the picture say TESTING: keep the engine inside the shadow line, plugged into a test setup, instrumentation leads and a sensor harness running back into the dark hangar, a test tag on the flange, the sunlit apron beyond empty, the two gold cases at the shade and sun line.

Craft and scale: fix the blocky mosaic on the left jamb and header, drop the camera lower and closer so engine and cases fill about half the frame, give the apron texture, joints and long first light shadows toward the camera, push the cases to true dusk gold with metal latches and edge wear.

Point 1 fails: a 3D waffle chart. Make the tray this deck flight record: a machined record cassette with a stamped plate (no mark), a data connector edge and a cable port. Show the 63 empty sockets as the damaged record (scorched, fractured, broken trace fragments), and the 37 gold blocks as restored segments engraved with a continuous flight data trace running across them.

Materials and seat: the tray reads as blue acrylic, the gold reads salmon, drop the hard dark blue wash band behind the type, bring the tray up and left to fill more of the frame and crop its far corner off the right edge. The count is correct.

Ground the tape lower run on the sweep with contact shadows, lifting only near the recorder. Replace the iridescent blobs with clean punched holes the key shines through throwing bright spots, plus two or three cells with charred brown edges. Fix the compressed middle run (y 1060 to 1150) where cells alias into slashes.
Give the recorder detail: a feed slot with lip and rollers where the tape exits, a bevelled faceplate with screws and a connector, edge wear on the fins, tint the black face toward indigo.

Raise Lubbock and Tarrant two to three times higher with bevelled rims and matching stone grain, rake the key low so counties, the route channel and the rivets throw long indigo shadows, seat each rivet in a countersunk collar.

Fix the bottom third: the footer wash greys the caliche and the south is cropped behind it. Lift the map to fill the empty blue above the Panhandle with the whole state, or crop tighter on the Lubbock to Fort Worth band so route, bosses and rivets are the hero.

Concept: a ruler with a clip could sit on any story. The machine material code must appear.

Craft: the stainless reads as blue plastic (chamfer, anisotropic brushing, indigo bevel reflection), polish and weather the brass stop with a contact shadow, move the 480 hour phase pill off the tab and away from the counter.

Make the flagged blade the subject: push the camera in and down so its leading edge runs diagonally through the middle third, the gold strip about three times thicker with a soft emissive bloom, a fine gold hairline root to tip with tick marks so tracks life becomes visible, other blades falling to indigo and soft focus.

Rebuild or crop out the hub and roots (flat orange zigzag roots, bare hex bolts, a blue void bore, moire hex casing). Drop the camera so the disc face and bore leave the frame, set the footer over calm indigo shadow, give the blades the straw to peacock heat tint and visible twist.
